newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Oil Search says Moran-3X results ambiguous.
newsitem.headline: Oil Search says Moran-3X results ambiguous.

text.p: Papua New Guinea oil producer Oil Search Ltd said on Tuesday that analysis of results from its Moran-3X Sidetrack 1 well suggested that oil present may be residual, despite substantial evidence for the presence of live oil.
Oil Search also said pressure information indicated that the Moran-3X well may be in a different fault compartment than the Moran-1X and 2X wells.
"Given the ambiguous nature of the results no definitive conclusion can be made on reservoir fluid content," Oil Search said in a drilling report.
Oil Search said the Moran-3X ST-1 well was drilling ahead at 2,652 metres and wireline logging had shown moderate to good oil shows, consistent with proven oil intersections in Moran-1X and Moran-2X.
There had been direct evidence of oil in the mud whilst drilling, underscored by gas wetness ratios indicating the presence of live oil in both the Toro and Digimu sandstones.
However, initial analysis of wireline logging and pressure information indicated oil present in both the Toro and Digimu sections may be residual in nature, it said.
"The nature of fluids present in the Toro and Digimu sections will be determined in a proposed testing programme planned at the end of initial drilling operations," it added.
Further analysis was being carried out to reconcile the results.
"Pressure information does indicate that the Moran-3X well is in a different fault compartment to that of the Moran-1X and 2X wells," Oil Search said.
Current drilling is planned to evaluate deeper reservoir objectives and obtain further structural information.
Oil Search shares slipped on the news and were trading down 38 cents at A$3.52 at 3.45 p.m. (0545 GMT).
Oil Search has a 35.017 percent interest in PPL-161 in which the Moran-3X well is being drilled.

Other participants are Chevron unit and operator Chevron Niugini Pty Ltd with 25.0 percent; Mobil Corp unit Ampolex (Highlands) Pty Ltd 21.233 percent; BHP Petroleum (PNG) Inc 12.5 percent and Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd unit Merlin Petroleum Co 6.25 percent.
